summary.headline: Indigo Paints Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 8.4% to INR397.9 crore; management signals margin sacrifice of 2-2.5pp to chase faster top-line growth.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue grew 8.4% YoY to INR397.9 crore, with EBITDA of INR91.7 crore (23.0% margin) and gross margin of 48.6% versus 47.4% a year earlier, despite raw material costs rising 50-100% in March 2026 due to the Middle East conflict. PAT fell to INR57.3 crore (14.4% margin) as treasury income dropped to INR0.19 crore on mark-to-market losses. For FY26, standalone revenue grew 4.1% to INR1,330 crore and PAT excluding a one-off gratuity provision grew 4% to INR149.8 crore. Management said it will accept roughly 200-250bp lower gross margin, with EBITDA margin broadly unchanged, to accelerate top-line growth in FY27. It also said no major capex is planned until FY29, with the Jodhpur water-based plant commissioning in June 2026.

segments.name: Paint categories (Q4 FY26 value growth / volume growth)
segments.commentary: Primers and distemper grew 14.9% value and 9.6% volume; putty and cement paint 12.6% value and 9.5% volume; emulsions 10.5% value and 11.2% volume; enamels and wood coatings 7.2% value and 5.4% volume. All four categories grew in value and volume.

segments.name: Apple Chemie (subsidiary, waterproofing)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR27.5 crore (+34.7% YoY); FY26 revenue INR75.1 crore (+17.8%). Gross margin around 40% plus/minus 1%. FY27 target is 30%-plus growth.

guidance_outlook: Management is prepared to accept a 2-2.5pp gross margin decline to drive faster top-line growth, while expecting EBITDA margin broadly unchanged.

Gross sales were growing double-digit for five consecutive months from November 2025, including March; the gap to reported net sales growth (8.5% in Q4) came from higher trade and influencer discounts netted off revenue.

Management said it is not guiding a specific net sales number for Q1 FY27 and expects net sales growth well above high-single-digit to low-double-digit levels over FY27, with the caveat that disruptions can set it back.
April growth was driven largely by price hikes; some dealer overstocking has occurred, so May-June demand is uncertain.
Industry price increases of about 12% on the overall basket were implemented; management does not foresee another significant price increase unless the Middle East situation deteriorates.
Management expects gross margins across the industry to normalise by Q2 FY27 as raw material costs stabilise, though Q1 may see volatility.
Apple Chemie targets 30%-plus revenue growth in FY27.
No major capex is envisaged until FY29; FCF is expected to step up from FY27 onwards. FY26 dividend proposed at INR5 per share, up 43% from INR3.5.
capex_capacity: Jodhpur water-based plant, 90,000 KL per annum capacity: final commissioning stage, trial production expected June 2026.
New solvent-based plant and expanded putty plant at Jodhpur have already commenced production in recent months.
Network at 31 March 2026: over 19,350 active dealers, over 12,200 tinting machines, 55 depots across all 28 states.
330 kW solar installation at Kochi factory is fully operational.
demand_pricing: Industry demand recovered from November 2025 after roughly 8 quarters of subdued growth; the Iran war from about March 2026 disrupted raw material supply and pushed some input prices up 50-100%.
The industry took about 12% price increases in three phases. Indigo's own unilateral price increase came around 24-25 March 2026, ahead of the market leader's 8 April increase.

Management said water-based paints are fully covered by price hikes; solvent-based enamels and wood coatings (about 17-18% of portfolio) have a small uncovered gap, partly offset by falling mineral turpentine oil prices.
Management said the competitive intensity has moderated over the last couple of quarters; it sees no change in behaviour since JSW's acquisition of Akzo.
Differentiated products make up about 30% of sales and are described as price-inelastic, so margin reduction is expected mainly in the other two-thirds of the portfolio.
Premium emulsions are a growing share; management said value growth has exceeded volume growth in almost all categories over the last 20 quarters or more.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Apple Chemie growth accelerate to 35% in Q4 and what are its margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was muted because government contractors' payments were delayed, but Q3 and Q4 grew about 30%-plus; gross margin is about 40% plus/minus 1%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company pursuing more aggressive market share gains, and will a 200bp gross margin sacrifice be enough to reach about 24% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: The Board judged the company had been too conservative on margins; it will spend more on trade schemes and influencers, lowering gross margin 2-2.5pp while EBITDA margin should hold. Management said yes, 24% growth is achievable.

qa_highlights.question: Where will the gross margin reduction come from, and is competition the reason?
qa_highlights.answer: Extra spend will be netted from revenue through trade discounts and influencer costs, mainly in non-differentiated products. Management said competitive intensity has normalised and the move reflects a wish to grow faster, not a response to competitors.

qa_highlights.question: Reconcile double-digit gross growth with single-digit reported growth, and will net sales be sacrificed?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross sales grew double-digit in each of the last five months, but higher trade and influencer discounts cut Q4 net growth to 8.5%. Management does not expect net sales growth to fall back to single digits.

qa_highlights.question: Will more price increases be needed, and how is pricing held if costs fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not expect another significant price increase unless the Middle East situation worsens. It said the company now acts independently on pricing and that margins should normalise by Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company growing in metros and dealer productivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Tier 1 and Tier 2 coverage is now good, and growth will come from deeper dealer throughput, not city size; with about 19,500 dealers it sees room to double sales per dealer.

risks_watch: Gross margin compression of 2-2.5pp from trade and influencer spending; watch whether EBITDA margin holds near 23%.
Gap between gross and net sales growth caused by rising discounts; watch Q1 FY27 net revenue.
Possible overstocking by dealers after April price-led growth; May-June demand is unclear.
Raw material volatility from the Middle East conflict; solvent-based products carry an uncovered cost gap.
Commissioning and ramp-up risk at the Jodhpur water-based plant, targeted for June 2026.
Apple Chemie's dependence on government-linked infrastructure payments, which were delayed in H1 FY26.
Treasury income is exposed to bond yield mark-to-market movements (Q4 FY26 treasury income was INR0.19 crore against INR5.6 crore a year earlier).
summary.management_tone: Confident and assertive on the growth ambition, with management stating an explicit intent to press for faster top-line growth. Cautious on the near term: it declined to give a Q1 net sales number and flagged overstocking and geopolitical risk.
key_quotes: We are in a phase where growing and gaining market share is the top priority.
we are prepared to accept some moderation in our gross margins if required.
We are not a company that has ever burned cash or come even remotely close to it.
we do not envisage any further major capex until FY '29.

adds.what: 90,000 KL per annum Jodhpur water-based paint plant

growth.why: Management expects net sales growth well above high-single to low-double digits over FY27 (no number given) and accepts a 200-250bp gross margin decline to drive it, backed by the 90,000 KL Jodhpur water-based plant in trial runs for June 2026, a 30%+ Apple Chemie growth target, and five months of double-digit gross sales growth; the net-sales guidance itself lacks a specific number or order book.
